prerequisites: Proficiency in the set of mathematical tools studied in previous courses, such as trigonometry, analytic geometry, functions of several variables, two- and three-dimensional integration, and at least linear differential equations.
Mastery of the skills acquired in Engineering Graphic Expression.

Proficiency in theoretical Mechanics, especially the part related to the kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies, both in plane and space, including the study of vector analysis and corresponding vectorial and analytical principles, due to considering mechanical elements as rigid inertial elements.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students are able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to kinematics and dynamics of Machines
teaching_methods: Theoretical explanations followed by practical applications in the form of exercises and problems
Careful reading of the Study Guide and progressive study of each chapter of the base text
Practice problem-solving and complete proposed activities
Use of digital teaching resources, including author's video lessons, mechanism simulation videos, and computational and simulation tools
Development of practices and exercises using common computational tools, such as spreadsheets
Participation in forums for exchanging and resolving doubts
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained from the formula: 0.9 * In-person exam score + 0.2 * Average PEC score. The PEC score is only taken into account if a minimum of 4 points is achieved in the in-person exam. For the in-person exam, obtaining the correct result for an section is required to pass it; a correct approach with a significant error in results may lead to no more than 40% of the maximum score for that section. If the final score exceeds 10 points, a score of 10 (Matrícula de honor) will be assigned. A third PEC may be proposed for students taking the September extraordinary session.
